title.narrative: Water Resources Management in Pyanj River Basin Project

description.narrative:
The Water Resources Management in the Pyanj River basin (PRB) Project will improve institutional and physical capacities of water resources management (WRM) system in PRB of southern Tajikistan, and it will: (i) establish a PRB organization, council, and Joint PRB committee, and develop a PRB management plan; (ii) modernize and climate-proof the Chubek Irrigation System (CIS); and (iii) improve farm and water use management capacities.
The impact of the proposed project will be increased farm income in the CIS area of PRB. The outcome will be increased agricultural water productivity in CIS area of PRB. The key outputs will be (i) WRM capacity improved in PRB; (ii) WRM infrastructure in PRB modernized and climate-proofed; (iii) farm management and water use capacities increased; and (iv) efficient and effective project management system. The installation of a sediment basin, the replacement of pumps and motors in the pump stations with energy efficient ones, and more profitable farm management to enable them to pay water use levies will result in more sustainable O&M of CIS.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative:
Ongoing project Agricultural production increased in CIS area of PRB Agricultural productivity and relevance of forecasting services increased in the PRB
Overall project Unchanged

Share of annual Hydromet budget contributed by income from sale of fee-based services increased Progress/Status: Hydromet is in the process of increasing its revenue by creating an IT system and subscription platform, as well as introducing new products. According to the financial analysis, the profitability of Hydromet has improved by 3 times compared to 2017. In the end of 2023, an analysis of the profitability of Hydromet was carried out. The results showed that the profitability due to the sale of paid Hydromet services increased by 6.7%. An ongoing profitability analysis was conducted in the first half of 2024. Source Q2 Progress report Hydromet. Data Source: Hydromet annual reports Actual value:

Crop yield increased by 8% (wheat [2.96 t/ha], cotton [2.05 t/ha], vegetables [21/00 t/ha], orchard [8.93 t/ha], fodder maize [19.00 t/ha]) Achievement: 15.6% Progress/Status: Achieved.
Main crop yield in CIS zone increased on average by 2019-2023: wheat - 4,21 t/ha; cotton - 2,16 t/ha; vegetables - 27,52 t/ha; orchard - 8,74 t/ha; fodder maize - 19,45 t/ha. Data Source: Provincial and district agricultural statistics, and NGOs' report through ALRI Target value: 108% Actual value: 15.6%

Cropping intensities increased by 10% for gravity irrigation and by 50% for pump irrigation Achievement: 17 and 48 Progress/Status: Substantially Achieved.
Cropping intensities as of December 1, 2023 increased to 17.3% on lands with gravity irrigation and to 47.7% on lands with pump irrigation in the CIS zone. Data Source: Provincial and district agricultural statistics, and NGOs' report through ALRI Target value: 110 and 150 Actual value: 17 and 48

Share of surveyed government and civil society stakeholders “satisfied” with Hydromet's forecasting services increased Progress/Status: The fourth phase of the survey was completed in April 2024. For this purpose, a contract was signed with NGO "Eco Loiha". During the survey 235 beneficiaries were involved. More than 35% of the respondents were women. The results of the survey showed that at the fourth stage of the survey 74% of the SHs stated that they were satisfied with the services provided by Hydromet. The Hydromet website is update. All information about the project activities is covered in three languages. A separate page for the project is open. source Q2 Progress Report. Data Source: Hydromet market survey reports Actual value:

Cultivated irrigated areas (hectares) served by CIS increased to originally designed Achievement: 49831 Progress/Status: Substantially Achieved.
Cultivated irrigated areas in CIS zone increased to 49,831 hectares by 2024 (367 hectares excluding irrigated lands of Kulyab district since the pumping stations supplying water to these lands have not been rehabilitated). Data Source: ALRI reports
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Farm management capacity and water use skill improved Indicator: Women's membership in WUAs increased Achievement: 31.4 Progress/Status: Achieved. As of December 31, 2022, an updated list of women members of the WUA has been received, which determines the number of its members (disaggregated by gender) and leadership. Thus, in 21 operating WUAs of the CIS zone, the total number of water user members was 49,231 people, of which 33,780 were men and 15,451 were women, which is 31.4%. Previously, only farms were considered WUA members. This list received from the WUA SU of ALRI for 3 (three) Project districts includes all water users, including those with presidential and leased lands, subsidiary plots, rural cooperatives, as well as household plots that receive irrigated water and pay for irrigation services through WUA. Data Source: NGO reports through ALRI

Output: Farm management capacity and water use skill improved Indicator: Average collection rate (in value terms) of irrigation service fee among all WUAs increased Achievement: 83.9 Progress/Status: Achieved. The average level of fee collection for irrigation services among all WUAs for 2022 was 78.9% (calculated on an annual basis). For 2023 was 83.9% (calculated on an annual basis). This indicator will be tracked until the completion of the Project and will reflect the influence of functioning SEB. Data Source: NGO reports through ALRI

Output: Modernized and climate-proofed CIS WRM infrastructure fully operational Indicator: Sediment entering CIS canal by m3/year reduced Achievement: 82117 m³/year Progress/Status: Achieved.
The construction of a sediment excluding basin is included in Package ICB-W-1 (Lot 1). The package was awarded in July 2020, and the works started on 20 September 2020. Construction works for this contract are completed. Activities for preparation of the Facility for tests and prior acceptance of the State Commission are ongoing.
Since the completion of the Sediment Excluding Basin (SEB) in Hamadoni district, from April 1, 2023 to March 31, 2024, observations of the volumes of sediment entering from the Pyanj River into the CIS canals have been carried out. Calculations of the obtained data on retained and washed away sediment showed that the volume of sediment entering the CIS canal was 82,117 m³/year. This was achieved because of: a) the use of a new design solution in construction of the SEB (increasing its size) b) flexible operation and maintenance of the SEB (due to the optimal schedule for cleaning settled sediments in the SEB, c) as well as the hydro-climatic conditions that have developed at this period). Data Source: ALRI and consultant reports Actual value: 82117 m³/year

Output: Farm management capacity and water use skill improved Indicator: Average water use ratio (i.e., field application efficiency) in CIS area increased Achievement: 59.4 Progress/Status: Achieved. A monitoring system for assessing the water use ratio is currently being developed. By 2024, this indicator has been pretty much achieved; the average water use coefficient in the CIS zone has been increased to 59.4%. Full achievement of the goal is expected after the completion of additional works on the SEB and M&R of 8 remaining pumping units at the targeted pumping stations and the transfer of these facilities into operation in June 2024. Data Source: ALRI reports

Output: Modernized and climate-proofed CIS WRM infrastructure fully operational Indicator: Pump efficiency of target pump stations in CIS increased Achievement: 75.1% Progress/Status: Achieved. Rehabilitation works of pump stations included in Package ICB-W-1 (Lot 2) were awarded in July 2020, started on September 2020, and completed in April 2022. Acceptance of facilities by the state commission was completed in June 2022.
The efficiency (capacity) of 28 Pumping units at 8 target pumping stations in Farkhor and Vose districts was increased to 75.1%. The total design pumping capacity of these pumps before M&R was 71,708 m3/h, and after M&R became 89,740 m3/h. The increase in capacity was 18032 m3/h = 25.1%. The energy efficiency of pumping units increased by 27.0%. The design consumption of electricity by pumps for supplying 1 m3 of water before M&R was 0.19 kW/h, and after M&R it was 0.14 kW/h. Thus, the amount of energy savings for the supply of 1 m3 water counted to 0.05 kW, which is 27.0% (0.05 kW / 0.19 kW)/100%. Data Source: ALRI and consultant reports Actual value: 75.1%

Output: Farm management capacity and water use skill improved Indicator: WUAs coverage of CIS area increased Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Achieved. All water users in the CIS area covered by WUAs in 2020. Coverage of WUAs in the CIS area as a result of reorganization of 20 existing WUAs and establishment of 1 new WUA in Hamadoni district based on the hydrological boundaries of irrigation networks with legal recognition of suspended irrigated lands. Data Source: NGO reports through ALRI

Output: Farm management capacity and water use skill improved Indicator: At least 30% of women lead demonstration plot activities Achievement: 34 Progress/Status: Achieved. 22 of the total 65 households (or 34%) of the demonstration plots are women. (ALRI and PIG has selected all the demo plots.) Data Source: NGOs' reports through ALRI Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: 34

Output: Farm management capacity and water use skill improved Indicator: IT platform for sale of Hydromet information and forecasting products established, including government-approved pricing plan Progress/Status: It system is delivered and installed. New products are developed. The process of product promotion is underway. The pricing plan for the maintenance and provision of Hydromet services is approved annually. To provide information from the platform, it is equipped with modern technologies. Information about Hydromet services is provided on a regular basis through the Hydromet website.
Data Source: Hydromet project reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: Y

Output: Farm management capacity and water use skill improved Indicator: Individuals (of which 30% are female) report increased knowledge on receiving and using weather forecasting products in the PRB Progress/Status: During the workshop-meetings in the pilot areas of the project, stakeholders became aware of the services of Hydromet and consultations were held regarding the introduction of new Hydromet products. Especially women from the stakeholders participated actively in the discussions11. In total 500 stakeholders were involved, of which 185 were women (37%). Data Source: Hydromet project reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2024 Target value: At least 500

Output: Modernized and climate-proofed CIS WRM infrastructure fully operational Indicator: Access to water for household use provided by installation of 12 water points along main canal and three water points along each target inter-farm canal Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved.
12 water supply points have been installed in 2020 along the main canal and 16 water points in 2020 along the targeted inter-farm canals. Data Source: ALRI and consultant reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Modernized and climate-proofed CIS WRM infrastructure fully operational Indicator: Irrigation conveyance efficiency for on-farm canal in CIS increased to 66% for gravity-fed system and 82% for pump-fed system Achievement: 65.5% and 81.5% Progress/Status: Substantially Achieved.
The M&R works at 8 pump stations in Farkhor and Vose were completed with following details: (i) Cleaning of sediment from the irrigation canals network along the Chubek Irrigation System with a length of 68,726 meters, including: in Hamadoni district - 40,822 meters, in Farkhor - 22,363 meters and in Vose - 5,541 meters; (ii) Concrete lining of canals with a volume of 2,002 m3 was made, including in Hamadoni district - 1,395 m3 and in Farkhor - 607 m3; (iii) 4 aqueducts have been rehabilitated, including in Hamadoni district - 3 units and in Farkhor - 1 unit.
By 2024, the efficiency of on-farm irrigation canals in the CIS zone (average annual values), taking into account the completion of works on M&R of 28 pumping units of 8 pumping stations in Farkhor and Vose districts, as well as the M&R of the irrigation infrastructure of 3 (three) Project districts in accordance with the data of SILI of the Project districts, gravity systems have been increased to 65.5% and for pump fed systems to 81.5%. Full efficiency will be achieved with the commissioning of the SEB and the remaining 8 pumping units at the targeted pumping stations Urtaboz and Janubi, after completion of additional works at these facilities. Data Source: ALRI and consultant reports Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: 60% for both systems Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: 60% for both systems Target year: 2024 Target value: 66% and 82% Actual value: 65.5% and 81.5%

Output: Water resources in PRB better managed Indicator: Hydromet transformed to state entity with right to seek, retain, and use additional commercial income Progress/Status: Resolution of the government was approved on 29 July 2022. Hydromet and consultant are working on the implementation of the resolution.
Mid-term review mission 21-26 July 2022: The draft Resolution was prepared and submitted to the Government, taking into account the changes and additions that were made by relevant departments.
According to the new Resolution, the organizational transformation has been completed. At the moment, there are 7 centers, 6 departments and 25 divisions in various areas of activity. Data Source: Government resolution or decision Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: Y

Output: Water resources in PRB better managed Indicator: Joint Afghanistan-Tajikistan PRB committee commences monitoring the Pyanj River water Achievement: N Progress/Status: The Government of Tajikistan decided to create working groups for the joint management of the Basin within the Intergovernmental Commission on Economic, Social and Technical Cooperation between Afghanistan and Tajikistan, established in 2017. In collaboration with MEWR, the mandate, regulations, and responsibilities for the Tajik working group were developed and approved by the Intergovernmental Commission in July 2020. Subsequently, MEWR agreed with the Afghanistan National Water Affairs Regulation Authority to convene a meeting in Dushanbe in August 2021 to discuss: (i) WG mandate and regulations; and (ii) a work plan for 2022.Due to change of the Afghanistan Government the meeting was postponed. Data Source: MEWR reports Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Water resources in PRB better managed Indicator: Local flood forecasts publicly issued for pilot PRB districts at least 36 hours in advance with >40% probability of detection and <25% false alarm rate. Progress/Status: By installation of SmartMet system, process of forecasting and preventing natural disasters will significantly improve. The number of probability of the flood forecast was 80%. The percentage of false alarms is 20%. The installation and training of the HEC HMS program, which were planned for the second quarter of 2023 by an international consultant, improved the forecasting and warning system, the percentage of probability and a reduction in the percentage of false alarms. Data Source: Hydromet project reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: Y

Output: Water resources in PRB better managed Indicator: New Hydromet operation center modernized with gender-sensitive facilities Progress/Status: Construction on main office building, laboratory building, warehouse, garage, information center and site landscaping completed.
Mid-term review mission 21-26 July 2022: Main building, laboratory, storage facilities, garage, information center buildings completed. Data Source: Hydromet project reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: Y

Output: Water resources in PRB better managed Indicator: PRBMP, including drought management plan, submitted to PRBC Achievement: Y Progress/Status: The PRBMP, including the basin drought management plan, was presented to the PRB Council and to the basin stakeholders at the TA completion workshop held on 24 Dec 2021. The workshop participants, including representatives of local authorities in the basin and PRB Council, endorsed the Plan. Data Source: MEWR reports Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Water resources in PRB better managed Indicator: PRBO and PRBC management structures each include at least one woman Achievement: Y Progress/Status: The PRBOs have been established and employed by MEWR in June 2020 including 3 women out of 12 staffs. The PRBC was established in December 2021. Data Source: MEWR reports Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Water resources in PRB better managed Indicator: Participants in stakeholder meetings in PRB Council are women Progress/Status: On average, between 10 and 12% of the participants of the PRB dialogues were women, the precursor to formation of the River Basin Council were women. Data Source: MEWR reports Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: 0% Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: 0% Target year: 2018 Target value: 30%

Output: Water resources in PRB better managed Indicator: Water discharge monitored at key sections of Pyanj River matches the actual diversions Progress/Status: Construction completed. Monitoring of water discharge at key sections vs actual diversions to be conducted. Data Source: MEWR reports Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y
